report.summary: Fixed the boot-blocking crash: the voice front end's dot product now runs on esp-dsp's generic C kernel (new app_dsp_shim component linked ahead of esp-dsp), so audio init completes and the dashboard, settings page, MQTT and console are reachable; the pinned broker CA is also persisted and clearable. Builds at 2.93 MB, 20 % free.
decisions: The functional failure was a real boot abort in esp-dsp's RISC-V assembly reached from esp-sr's prebuilt front end. The report's suggested Kconfig path (CONFIG_DSP_ANSI) was tried first and is wrong for this tree: esp-sr's c_speech_features is a prebuilt archive that calls dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 by name, so ANSI mode makes it an undefined reference (verified by the failing link).

Root cause therefore: the symbol is baked into a prebuilt library while its only optimized implementation faults on this target. Fix at that boundary — a small component (app_dsp_shim) that defines the same symbol with esp-dsp's ANSI implementation, ordered before esp-dsp so the linker never reaches the assembly member. One kernel replaced, everything else in esp-dsp keeps its optimized code.
Also folded in the review's non-blocking note: the pinned broker CA is now persisted in NVS and can be cleared with a lone '-', so it survives reboots and cannot get stuck.
report.build: esp32s31 success — 0x2cc6e0 (2934496 B) in a 0x380000 partition, 20% free; check_code clean on the 3 edited sources

findingsAddressed.finding: fail — boot aborts with illegal/misaligned instruction in dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 (esp-dsp) during wake-word feature extraction, so nothing after app_audio_init runs
findingsAddressed.fix: generic C dsps_dotprod_f32_arp4 in the new app_dsp_shim component, linked ahead of esp-dsp (CONFIG_DSP_ANSI tried first and rejected: the prebuilt esp-sr archive requires the symbol)

findingsAddressed.finding: warning — pinned CA not persisted, cannot be cleared from the page
findingsAddressed.fix: CA stored in NVS 'ca' and restored by mqtt_load_config(); a lone '-' in the settings field clears it (erases the key, falls back to the built-in pack); CA-only edits rebuild the session

openQuestions: Whether esp-dsp's other hardware-loop kernels (FFT, FIR, biquad, matrix) also fault on this target is untested here; the wake-word path only needed the dot product, and an FFT fault would show up in the next functional run if it exists.
The same class of fault may be an emulator gap rather than silicon; the shim is safe on both (identical arithmetic), so it is not reverted.
